record.paper_title: Open Problems within Nonextensive Statistical Mechanics
record.original_question: What is the proper normalization of a generalized entropy in NSM, and how does the chosen normalization affect the relationship between generalized entropy and statistical degrees of freedom? A satisfactory criterion should address why normalized Tsallis entropy was rejected for stability reasons, why normalized and unnormalized Tsallis entropy do not account for the way derivatives from cumulative distribution functions to probability density functions affect generalized exponential and logarithmic definitions and probability-density structure, and why the nonlinear term combining coupled entropy is the inverse of statistical degrees of freedom.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6: What is the proper normalization of a generalized entropy and how does the normalization impact the relationship between a generalized entropy and the statistical degrees of freedom? Stability issues caused a rejection of the normalized Tsallis entropy;

however , neither the normalized nor unnormalized Tsallis entropy considers how the derivatives of a cdf into a pdf impacts the relationship between the definition of the generalized exponential and logarithmic functions and the structure of a pdf and its generalized entropy. When this is accounted for the nonlinear term combining a nonextensive entropy (coupled entropy) is precisely the inverse of the statistical degrees of freedom. Does this suggest a criterion for the normalization?

A careful analysis of whether the difference in normalization impacts the performance improvements would contribute to determining the importance of the normalization. Entropic analysis has been shown to be an effective measure of financial market volatility but greater detail is needed to determine the relative advantages of different forms of generalized entropy [63,64].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. For a discrete probability distribution $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^W$ with $p_i\ge 0$, $\sum_i p_i=1$, and a real deformation parameter $q$ (equivalently the nonlinear statistical coupling $\kappa$ related to $q$ by $q=1+\kappa$ or analogous reparametrizations), one defines:

- the (unnormalized) Tsallis entropy
$$S_q(p)=\frac{1-\sum_i p_i^{q}}{q-1},$$
- the normalized Tsallis entropy
$$S_q^{N}(p)=\frac{1-\sum_i p_i^{q}}{(q-1)\sum_i p_i^{q}},$$
- the deformed exponential and logarithm
$$\exp_q(x)=[1+(1-q)x]_+^{1/(1-q)},\qquad \ln_q(x)=\frac{x^{1-q}-1}{1-q},$$
- and, for a continuous probability density function $f$ obtained as the derivative of a cumulative distribution function $F$, the corresponding continuous versions of $S_q$ and $S_q^{N}$.

A "coupled entropy" $S^{C}_\kappa(p)$ is constructed from $S_q$ by a nonlinear (coupled) combination of the entropies of independent subsystems whose nonlinear additivity term equals $1/d$, where $d$ denotes the effective statistical degrees of freedom of the system.

Problem. Formulate and justify a normalization criterion $\mathcal{N}$ for a generalized entropy of the above family which simultaneously satisfies all of the following:

1. $\mathcal{N}$ avoids the Lesche-type instability that led to the rejection of the normalized Tsallis entropy $S_q^{N}$.
2. $\mathcal{N}$ incorporates how the passage from a cumulative distribution function to its probability density (i.e., differentiation $F\mapsto f$) constrains the consistent definitions of $\exp_q$, $\ln_q$, and the resulting form of the entropy functional on densities — a constraint not respected by either $S_q$ or $S_q^{N}$.
3. Under $\mathcal{N}$, the nonlinear coupling term appearing in the additivity rule for the coupled entropy of independent subsystems is exactly $1/d$, where $d$ is the statistical degrees of freedom.

Determine the explicit normalized functional form of the generalized entropy satisfying (1)–(3), and prove that this normalization is uniquely characterized (up to admissible reparametrizations) by these requirements. In particular, establish the precise relationship between the normalization constant and the statistical degrees of freedom $d$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of selecting the correct normalization of generalized (Tsallis-type) entropies and tying it to statistical degrees of freedom remains under active investigation. Recent work (2025) on the "coupled entropy" proposes that the coupled entropy is the appropriate normalization because its nonlinear additivity term equals 1/d, but a definitive normalization criterion and uniqueness theorem have not been established. The problem is stated as an open problem in the survey on nonextensive statistical mechanics and is still being addressed in follow-up papers.

status_evidence.title: Coupled Entropy: A Goldilocks Generalization for Complex Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Only the coupled entropy converges to the scale as the coupling increases; normalized Tsallis entropy is 'too hot' and unnormalized Tsallis entropy fails to be a metric.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work proposes the coupled entropy as the proper normalization, but the criterion remains under development.

status_evidence.title: On the uniqueness of the coupled entropy
status_evidence.snippet: Investigation of uniqueness properties of the coupled entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of the coupled-entropy normalization is still being investigated.
